text:
sophie_support: Hi — customer on a private VPC running the onprem installer. Installer fails when pulling deps and model shards. Error in installer log: 

```
  ERROR: TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (while accessing https://packages.redwood-inference.com/artifactory/pypi/simple/)
  failed to download shard metadata from https://models.redwood-inference.net/shards/abc123/metadata.json: TLS alert: certificate_unknown
```

sophie_support: They also see 502s from the runtime during startup and frequent 403s hitting auth.redwood-inference.com when fetching tokens. Customer is strict on egress allowlist — can we supply a minimal host+port list and any special SNI/OCSP/mTLS notes?

raj_ops: which OS/container image and do you have full verbose curl output from the node that fails? also are they doing TLS interception (corporate proxy)?

sophie_support: Ubuntu 22.04 minimal cloud image, straight NAT via customer-managed NATGW (no proxy), split-horizon DNS in their VPC. here's the curl -v that reproduces the cert issue:

```
  curl -v https://packages.redwood-inference.com/artifactory/pypi/simple/ --connect-timeout 10
  * About to connect() to packages.redwood-inference.com port 443 (#0)
  * TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
  * TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
  * TLS certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
  * Closing connection 0
  curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

luis_infra: thanks — common issues here: (1) split-horizon can return an internal cert chain that the node can't validate; customer must allow OCSP/CRL checks to our OCSP responder and not intercept TLS. (2) model shards are served from a CDN with ephemeral hostnames behind models.redwood-inference.net — those hostnames resolve to many IPs and can be rotated. We recommend allowing FQDNs (SNI-aware) instead of fixed IPs when possible.

luis_infra: Minimal outbound allowlist we typically ask for (TCP 443 unless noted):

```
  packages.redwood-inference.com   # artifactory + pypi
  auth.redwood-inference.com       # oauth/token exchange
  telemetry.redwood-inference.com  # metrics/heartbeat (HTTPS)
  models.redwood-inference.net     # model registry + shards (CDN)
  ocsp.redwood-inference.com       # OCSP responder for our cert chain
  kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com      # (if using S3-backed model storage)
  sts.amazonaws.com                # token exchange for cloud pulls
  acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org:80  # if installer needs ACME HTTP challenge
```

luis_infra: Important notes: allow outbound TCP 443 to those hostnames with SNI preserved; if the customer does TLS MITM (proxy), it will break cert validation and OCSP. For model shards we either allow the FQDN wildcard `*.models.redwood-inference.net` or allow the CDN ASN ranges — wildcard is easier. Also ensure DNS resolves external names (split-horizon should forward unknown zones).

jamie_ml: additional item — the runtime will attempt to download a small token file from `auth.redwood-inference.com/.well-known/jwks.json` and then call model registry with a bearer token. If the customer blocks `auth` it shows up as 403s and then the runtime falls back to a lower-capacity variant which looks like a 502 at the app layer.

deploy-bot: Installer attempt 2146254310: stage=fetch-models, status=error, err="certificate_unknown"

raj_ops: can you try a targeted reproduce with `curl --resolve` to force the external IP and show SNI mismatch? e.g. `curl -v --resolve packages.redwood-inference.com:443:52.11.22.33 https://packages.redwood-inference.com/` — paste output if available.

sophie_support: did that, here's the snippet showing SNI mismatch when the customer's split-horizon returned a private IP with internal cert:

```
  curl -v --resolve packages.redwood-inference.com:443:10.0.0.5 https://packages.redwood-inference.com/
  * Connected to packages.redwood-inference.com (10.0.0.5) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS 1.3 handshake completed with certificate CN=internal-ca.local
  * Server certificate common name (CN) does not match 'packages.redwood-inference.com'
  * SSL: certificate subject name 'internal-ca.local' does not match target host name 'packages.redwood-inference.com'
```

luis_infra: that confirms split-horizon returning internal certs. Options: have them return the public cert chain for that hostname, or configure the VPC DNS to forward that FQDN to an external resolver for those nodes, or we can provide a short-lived IP allowlist (not recommended long-term). For escalation: networking team will need to confirm NAT egress SNAT behavior and whether they run TLS inspection appliances.

raj_ops: i'll open a networking ticket and ask for reachability tests. can you give me a single-line minimal list I can paste into the ticket? also include ports and a note about SNI/OCSP.

luis_infra: sure — one-liner below (comma-separated):

packages.redwood-inference.com:443, auth.redwood-inference.com:443, telemetry.redwood-inference.com:443, models.redwood-inference.net:443, ocsp.redwood-inference.com:443, kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com:443, sts.amazonaws.com:443, acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org:80

sophie_support: perfect, pasted. customer asked if we can provide a temporary static IP list while they update DNS rules — can you generate a short-lived CIDR/ips?

luis_infra: we can provide an ad-hoc set of IPs for 72h for troubleshooting but stress that those IPs will change for the CDN. i'll escalate to netops and request the troubleshooting IPs and an ops runbook (will post here when I have them).

sophie_support: thanks — i'll keep the customer updated and attach the curl outputs. :thumbsup:

raj_ops: assigning to netops for IPs + DNS checklist. tagging @netops (via ticket).

luis_infra: also adding a short repro for them to run on a failing node:

```
  # check DNS resolution for the FQDNs
  dig +short packages.redwood-inference.com
  dig +short models.redwood-inference.net

  # test TLS chain and OCSP
  openssl s_client -servername packages.redwood-inference.com -connect packages.redwood-inference.com:443 -status

  # test token exchange
  curl -v https://auth.redwood-inference.com/.well-known/jwks.json
```

sophie_support: got it, thanks everyone. i'll follow up once netops posts IPs or the customer updates DNS.
